The per-fill P&L and equity-curve metrics, the per-window return statistics, the transaction-cost model, and the report assembly all ended up tangled inside a few catch-all modules under marketlab/core/ and marketlab/util/, reached through an indirection layer that renames everything. Adding or changing one concern means touching that shared pile and the name mapping.

Reorganize this logic into clear, single-responsibility modules at these canonical paths: marketlab/backtest.py (net_pnl and the equity-curve compute_metrics), marketlab/metrics.py (mean_return, win_rate, max_drawdown_from_returns), marketlab/costs.py (the trade_costs model and its CostBreakdown), and marketlab/reports.py (build_report). Keep marketlab/__init__.py as the public entrypoint that re-exports the same API under the same public names. The observable behavior and the public API must not change.
issue_title: Evaluation reporting code is hard to extend after a migration collapsed unrelated logic together
issue_body:
The evaluation reporting code is hard to extend after a migration collapsed unrelated logic together. The per-fill P&L and equity-curve metrics, the per-window return statistics, the transaction-cost model, and the report assembly all ended up tangled inside a few catch-all modules under marketlab/core/ and marketlab/util/, reached through an indirection layer that renames everything. Adding or changing one concern means touching that shared pile and the name mapping.

Reorganize this logic into clear, single-responsibility modules at these canonical paths: marketlab/backtest.py (net_pnl and the equity-curve compute_metrics), marketlab/metrics.py (mean_return, win_rate, max_drawdown_from_returns), marketlab/costs.py (the trade_costs model and its CostBreakdown), and marketlab/reports.py (build_report). Keep marketlab/__init__.py as the public entrypoint that re-exports the same API under the same public names. The observable behavior and the public API must not change.
expected_behavior: Each concern lives in its own focused module at its canonical path: P&L and equity metrics in marketlab/backtest.py, per-window statistics in marketlab/metrics.py, the cost model in marketlab/costs.py, and report assembly in marketlab/reports.py.
Behavior is unchanged: net P&L, the equity-curve metrics, per-window return statistics, the cost breakdown, and the assembled report all produce the same results as before.
marketlab/__init__.py keeps exporting the same functions under the same public names, so existing callers do not change how they import.
The catch-all modules and the renaming indirection layer are gone.
expected_failure_summary: Backtest, metrics, cost, and report logic are collapsed into opaque catch-all modules reached via a renaming indirection layer; the canonical per-concern modules do not exist, so behaviour cannot be imported at its expected location.
task_author_notes: Broken collapses backtest/metrics/costs/reports into core/a.py (pnl+metrics+window stats), core/b.py (cost object+report), util/misc.py (cost components) plus a core/registry.py barrel that maps short internal names to the public names, with __init__/evaluation/cli routed through the barrel. A correct reorg relocates each concern to its canonical module AND re-exports under the correct public names via __init__.py, satisfying both the hidden behaviour tests and the structure contract.
